title: Choir and Garden
premise: Mara Sterling, a beast-speaker who has spent years guiding smugglers through the Thornfell mountains to stay beneath the Wardens' notice, discovers their own face and name in the Vellum Codex, a century-old book of prophecies hidden in a dead prophet's garden. The codex foretells that the 'Beast-Tongued Heir' will either renew or destroy the ancient pact between humans and the mountain's wild spirits, and both the Crown's Wardens and the exiled spirit-court are hunting for them. Forced into an uneasy found family of smugglers, a disgraced Warden, and a half-spirit guide, Mara must decide whether inheritance is a destiny to accept or a burden to refuse. In the end, Mara rewrites the prophecy itself—speaking not the words written for them but their own—sealing a new pact that frees the spirits without war, though it costs them their gift and leaves them, at last, simply human among people who chose to stay.
about_author: Xanthe Pemberton is the pen name of a former choir singer turned gardener who writes fantasy from a cottage overrun with herbs she refuses to weed. Her novels are known for prickly protagonists, talking animals with strong opinions, and endings that trade spectacle for quiet, hard-won grace.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Toll
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara guides a smuggler caravan through a Warden patrol by bargaining with mountain goats, revealing their forbidden beast-speech and their careful, invisible life. Emotional beat: competence masking loneliness; Mara helps everyone and belongs to no one.

chapters.title: A Date with the Dead
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. On a rare night off, Mara meets Ilex, a charming botanist, in the ruins of Prophet Sable's overgrown garden. When Ilex opens a buried ledger—the Vellum Codex—Mara sees their own name inked a century ago. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Ink Older Than Bone
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV. Ilex confesses they sought Mara deliberately, having recognized the prophecy's description of a beast-speaker born under the Thornfell sign. Their flirtation was reconnaissance—or so they claim. Emotional beat: betrayal tangled with genuine tenderness; neither can tell which came first.

chapters.title: What the Wardens Burn
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Warden Captain Odile Vess raids the smugglers' camp seeking the codex, burning the waystation where Mara grew up. Old mentor Bram dies covering Mara's escape. Emotional beat: grief and guilt; invisibility has failed, and people pay for it.

chapters.title: The Court of Roots and Teeth
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Fleeing uphill, Mara is taken by the exiled spirit-court, who confirm the prophecy: the Beast-Tongued Heir will renew or sever the ancient pact. Queen Briarthorn offers alliance—and a leash. Emotional beat: awe and manipulation; being chosen feels like being owned.

chapters.title: Company of Strays
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotation (Mara, Ilex, smuggler twins Fen and Rook). The fugitives regroup in a hollow tree inn run by Hesper, a disgraced Warden healer. Grudging alliances form over shared wounds. Emotional beat: the first stirrings of found family, defended with sarcasm.

chapters.title: Hesper's Ledger
chapters.summary: Hesper's POV. Hesper reveals why she left the Wardens: she once refused an order to burn a spirit-child, and the codex names her too—as 'the traitor who opens the door.' Emotional beat: shame transformed into resolve; the past becomes a map forward.

chapters.title: Goats Know Best
chapters.summary: Fen's POV. The twins test Mara's gift and loyalty by leading them through goat-trails only beasts know. A landslide nearly kills Rook; Mara speaks the mountain calm. Emotional beat: trust earned in rockfall; the twins stop calling Mara 'the cargo.'

chapters.title: Vess Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Odile Vess's POV. Vess interrogates Ilex's old letters and realizes the botanist is her former protégé. She offers Ilex amnesty to betray the group. Emotional beat: cold ambition shadowed by loneliness; Vess genuinely believes order saves lives.

chapters.title: The Garden Speaks
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Returning to Sable's garden, Mara learns the prophet was also a beast-speaker who wrote the codex as a warning, not a command—and that the final page is blank, waiting. Emotional beat: inheritance reframed; prophecy as invitation, not sentence.

chapters.title: Amnesty
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV. Cornered by Vess, Ilex pretends to accept betrayal while feeding false routes—but Vess anticipated the double-cross and lets them go, knowing they'll lead her true. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into determination; love used as bait.

chapters.title: The Hollow Bridge
chapters.summary: Rook's POV. Crossing a spirit-toll bridge, the group must each surrender a truth. Mara admits they've known how to end the pact since childhood and stayed silent out of fear. Emotional beat: confession as toll; secrets become shared weight.

chapters.title: Briarthorn's Bargain
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The spirit-queen demands Mara speak the Severance—a spell that would free spirits by dooming Thornfell's villages. Refusal means the court turns to older, crueler allies. Emotional beat: coercion dressed as honor; justice outside any law now has a body count.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: Fen's POV. Vess burns the hollow tree inn; Hesper is captured protecting the codex. The family scatters, and Fen blames Mara's hesitation. Emotional beat: fracture; found family tested by loss and recrimination.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Door
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV. Fulfilling the prophecy's line, Ilex opens Hesper's cell using her stolen Warden seal, freeing her at terrible cost—exposure of the whole conspiracy. Emotional beat: redemption through sacrifice; the 'traitor' name reclaimed as fidelity.

chapters.title: Two Armies, One Mountain
chapters.summary: Odile Vess's POV. Vess marches on the spirit-court's heart with fire-cant weapons, while Briarthorn summons the old powers below. Both sides believe prophecy licenses them. Emotional beat: tragic momentum; everyone reading the same book toward war.

chapters.title: The Blank Page
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At the garden's heart, Mara understands Sable's design: the blank page awaits the heir's own words, and speaking them requires giving up the gift entirely. Emotional beat: terror and clarity; the choice between power and personhood made plain.

chapters.title: Choir of Beasts
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. As armies collide, every creature Mara ever spoke with arrives—not commanded, but choosing—forming a living choir between the lines. Emotional beat: awe; the mountain itself takes a side, and it is Mara's.

chapters.title: Words of My Own
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Climax. Between Vess's fire and Briarthorn's roots, Mara writes and speaks their own terms of pact—neither renewal nor severance but coexistence with accountability. The codex accepts the words; the old magic dissolves. Emotional beat: self-authorship; destiny answered with authorship.

chapters.title: The Quiet After
chapters.summary: Hesper's POV. Vess, stripped of certainty rather than life, surrenders when her soldiers hear the new pact sung by the land itself. Briarthorn withdraws to negotiate. Emotional beat: exhaustion and mercy; victory that refuses vengeance.

chapters.title: Silence Where the Song Was
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The gift is gone; goats are just goats. Mourning the loss, Mara finds the family stayed anyway—Ilex, the twins, Hesper—choosing them without the magic. Emotional beat: grief braided with belonging; loved for self, not function.

chapters.title: Planting Season
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Epilogue. The group restores Sable's garden together, planting the codex's pages as mulch for something new. Mara teaches children ordinary animal husbandry and keeps one blank notebook of their own. Emotional beat: rooted hope; inheritance passed on, rewritten, alive.
